description: "Recording experiment configurations, code versions, metrics, and artifacts so machine-learning runs can be compared and reproduced."
term: "Tracking (Experiment)"
letter: "T"

difficulty: "Intermediate"

## Simple explanation

Experiment tracking is keeping an organized record of model-training and
evaluation runs. It helps a team remember which data, code, settings, and
results produced each model.

## Technical explanation

An experiment tracker records metadata such as hyperparameters, metrics,
source revision, dataset and artifact identifiers, environment details, and
output files. Tracking systems may support comparisons, lineage, model
registry workflows, and collaboration.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Without reliable records, teams can lose the ability to reproduce results,
compare candidates, or identify regressions. Tracking also supports audits
and helps connect a deployed model to its training evidence.

## How it works

At the start of a run, the training job records its configuration and
identifiers. During execution it logs metrics and artifacts; after the run,
the team reviews and compares results. Sensitive data and credentials
should not be logged as artifacts or parameters.

## Practical example

A training workflow can record the Git commit, dataset version, learning
rate, validation metrics, and final checkpoint for each run. A later
engineer can inspect the run record to reproduce or explain the selected
model.

## Common misconceptions

- Logging a metric alone does not make an experiment reproducible; data,
  code, environment, and randomness can also matter.
- An experiment-tracking service is not automatically a model registry or
  full deployment-management system.
